```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", width = 88)
library(readNBS)
```

Many NBS release panels expose a dataset identity, dimensions, and a finite
set of combinations actually published by NBS. `readNBS` models those concepts
separately so selections follow published combinations instead of synthesizing
unsupported Cartesian products.

## Browse the dataset catalogue

`nbs_dataset_catalogue()` is a local metadata operation. It describes source
vintage, frequency, expected reporting geometry, and the route used by the
dataset loader:

```{r catalogue}
datasets <- nbs_dataset_catalogue("en")
yearbook_datasets <- datasets[
  grepl("YEARBOOK", datasets$dataset_id, fixed = TRUE),
  c("dataset_id", "title", "frequency", "route", "source_vintage"),
  drop = FALSE
]
yearbook_datasets
```

The catalogue may contain portal-backed panels, retained release tables,
Yearbook snapshots, and longitudinal collections. The `route` and
`source_vintage` columns identify local versus portal-backed acquisition paths
and should be read together.

## Inspect dimensions and valid tuples

For the CPI detail panel, dimensions are represented as rows with machine
values, display labels, validity dates, units, and semantics:

```{r dimensions}
cpi_detail <- "NBS/CN/M/CPI/PRICE_DETAIL"
dimensions <- nbs_dataset_dimensions(cpi_detail, language = "en")
dimensions[
  dimensions$dimension %in% c("category", "comparison", "residence"),
  c("dimension", "value", "label_en", "unit_en", "semantics"),
  drop = FALSE
]
```

The authoritative combinations are returned by
`nbs_dataset_valid_tuples()`. The `dimension_key` is a canonical, encoded
representation suitable for joins, caches, or saved specifications:

```{r tuples}
cpi_tuples <- nbs_dataset_valid_tuples(cpi_detail)
head(cpi_tuples, 6L)

chosen <- list(
  category = "headline",
  comparison = "yoy_index",
  residence = "national"
)
nbs_dimension_key(chosen)
```

The `dimension_key` is a readable semantic selector suitable for joins,
caches, logs, or saved specifications; portal UUIDs remain transport
identifiers.

## Resolve a descriptor before fetching

`nbs_resolve_dataset_series()` checks a filter against the valid tuple table
and returns the descriptor that will govern a fetch. This is useful when a
report should record the exact title, unit, source route, and manifest version
before retrieving observations:

```{r resolve}
descriptor <- nbs_resolve_dataset_series(cpi_detail, chosen, language = "en")
descriptor[c(
  "dataset_id", "dimension_key", "title_en", "unit_en", "frequency",
  "period_policy", "aggregation_basis", "route", "source_vintage",
  "manifest_version"
)]
```

Invalid combinations produce typed conditions, preserving the published tuple
contract. For example, a filter containing an unknown category reports:

```{r invalid-filter}
invalid <- tryCatch(
  nbs_resolve_dataset_series(
    cpi_detail,
    list(
      category = "not_published",
      comparison = "yoy_index",
      residence = "national"
    )
  ),
  error = function(error) {
    c(class = class(error)[[1L]], message = conditionMessage(error))
  }
)
invalid
```

`nbs_dataset_valid_tuples()` is the authoritative selector table. Independent
member lists can create combinations that NBS never published, particularly
for dependent dimensions, source-table eras, and sparse historical panels.

## Fetch a small retained panel leaf

The following Yearbook dataset is an installed official snapshot. It is a
small, deterministic panel leaf. The transport guard confirms local execution:

```{r retained-panel}
yearbook_id <- "NBS/CN/A/YEARBOOK_DEMOGRAPHY_LEGACY"
yearbook_filters <- list(series = "yb_27885efbbca702a7")
offline <- nbs_client(
  transport = function(...) stop("The retained panel attempted a network request."),
  retries = 0L
)

population <- nbs_fetch_dataset(
  yearbook_id,
  filters = yearbook_filters,
  client = offline
)
population[c(
  "dataset_id", "series", "value", "period", "source_yearbook",
  "source_table", "source_url", "source_vintage", "route"
)]
```

The returned data frame adds the source-table columns needed by a panel row
while retaining the common `date`, `period`, reporting-geometry, and
provenance fields. Treat the Yearbook row as a 2010 vintage and keep it
distinct from later population communiqué series.

## A panel workflow for live data

The same metadata-first pattern applies to a portal-backed dataset. A live
operation should be explicit in an application and should keep the requested
filters and descriptor with the resulting observations:

```{r live-panel, eval=TRUE}
if (interactive()) {
  panel_id <- "NBS/CN/M/CPI/PRICE_DETAIL"
  panel_filters <- list(
    category = "headline",
    comparison = "yoy_index",
    residence = "national"
  )
  panel <- nbs_fetch_dataset(
    panel_id,
    filters = panel_filters,
    start = "2025-01",
    end = "2025-12",
    client = nbs_client(timeout = 15, retries = 2L)
  )
  head(panel[c("period", "value", "unit", "source_vintage")])
}
```

The public portal uses anonymous HTTPS access when the network is available.
The client validates response shape, UUID mapping, and panel cardinality and
reports typed errors when a source contract changes.

For transformations and source-vintage decisions, continue to
[Provenance and reporting calendars](provenance-reporting-calendars.html).
